subject: DPA and telemetry/embeddings role clarification — signing path
messages:
From: Sophie Reynolds <sophie.reynolds@acme-payments.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: DPA redline + clarification on logs, embeddings & subprocessors

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal here at Acme asked me to get the DPA conversation moving so we can close procurement before year-end. Two quick items we need from Redwood to complete our review and route signature: 

1) Can you provide your latest DPA redline (we received v3 from sales but would like a clean redline showing controller/processor language and telemetry exceptions)?
2) We need definitive language on telemetry/logs retention and the scope of "operational telemetry" — specifically whether model embeddings and embedding request/response content are treated as logs or customer data.
3) Subprocessor inventory: please confirm current subprocessors and whether any EU transfers require SCCs or other legal mechanisms.

If possible, please include a short summary we can attach to our procurement packet (1-2 bullets per item). We would prefer to execute via DocuSign; send the envelope link when ready.

Best,
Sophie Reynolds
Senior Counsel, Acme Payments
Sophie.Reynolds@acme-payments.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sophie Reynolds <sophie.reynolds@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA redline + clarification on logs, embeddings & subprocessors

Sophie —

Thanks — looping in Laura (legal) and Priyom (privacy/infra) to get concrete language. Attached is the current redline we proposed internally (Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.docx) and our up-to-date subprocessor list (subprocessor_inventory_2025.csv).

High-level answers up front to help your packet:
- Controller vs Processor: Redwood is prepared to sign as processor for API-hosting customers; where customers host models in private deployments we propose controller responsibilities stay with the customer. We’ll propose explicit text to make that boundary clear.
- Telemetry vs Customer Content: By default: operational telemetry (metrics, system traces, error logs) is treated as service data; embeddings and request/response payloads are customer content and subject to the data handling protections in the DPA. We will propose language to exclude ephemeral, low-level kernel traces used solely for runtime performance.
- Subprocessors & transfers: Current subprocessors include cloud infra providers and a managed logging provider. For EU transfers, we rely on SCCs for subprocessors where needed; we'll include a clause that we will provide SCCs or equivalent on request and update the inventory before signature.

Next steps: Laura will propose specific clause edits and Priyom will confirm telemetry/embeddings retention windows and technical mitigations (e.g., encryption at rest for embeddings). After we agree, I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and share the link.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Sophie Reynolds <sophie.reynolds@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA redline + clarification on logs, embeddings & subprocessors

Thanks — quick tech note from infra/privacy: 

1) Embeddings: we treat embeddings as derived customer data. They are stored encrypted at rest in customer-specific buckets when using hosted API, and in customer-managed storage for Private deployments. Retention: default 30 days for cache entries, 90 days for persistent embeddings unless customer requests a different retention policy. We can surface a retention setting in the console for enterprise accounts.

2) Telemetry/logs: operational logs (CPU/GPU metrics, runtime traces, error logs with no PII) are aggregated and stored for a rolling 30-day window for performance and SLO purposes. Kernel-level traces that would reveal model internals are not collected persistently. 

3) Subprocessors: inventory attached. For any subprocessors that involve EU data handling we will add SCC reference and notify Acme 30 days prior to onboarding. We are open to a limited notification and review period for new subprocessors that will touch customer data.

Suggested minimal language to include in the DPA: 
"Customer data (including embeddings and derivative artifacts) remains Customer Data; Redwood will not use Customer Data to train models or improve model weights. Operational telemetry that cannot be associated with Customer Data may be used by Redwood solely to operate and secure the service"

Happy to jump on a 20-min sync if you want to talk specifics.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Sr. Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.inference.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Sophie Reynolds <sophie.reynolds@acme-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA redline + clarification on logs, embeddings & subprocessors

Sophie / team —

I've reviewed Marcus and Priyom's notes and completed a clean set of proposed DPA edits. Key calls I've made in the redline: 

- Controller/Processor: retained a clear split that defaults Redwood to Processor for hosted services; added a short schedule that customers complete to document Private deployments where different roles apply.
- Embeddings: added an explicit definition in Section 1.2 that treats embeddings and other derived vectors as Customer Data, with a carve-out that ephemeral cache entries (less than 24 hours) are operational cache and subject to shorter retention.
- Telemetry: clarified "Operational Telemetry" definition and added a limitation that telemetry will not include customer prompt/response payloads nor embeddings unless explicitly consented to.
- Subprocessors & Transfers: included language adding SCCs for EU transfers and a 30-day notice for new subprocessors that will access Customer Data.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.docx (clean markup), and a small signoff checklist for execution. Once Acme confirms language we will prepare DocuSign. Laura also notes an optional clause if Acme prefers export controls and EU-specific audit rights — let us know.

If this aligns, Marcus: please create the DocuSign envelope and select the signatory order (Acme signs first / Redwood countersigns). I'll prepare the final sign-off playbook.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com
From: Sophie Reynolds <sophie.reynolds@acme-payments.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2025 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA redline + clarification on logs, embeddings & subprocessors

Laura / Marcus —

This looks good and addresses our main concerns. Two follow-ups before we route to procurement: 

1) Please add a short note in the DPA (1-2 lines) confirming Redwood will not use Customer Data or embeddings to improve model weights or for model training.
2) We need an explicit SCC reference for subprocessors handling EU data (a clause or a link to the SCCs we can file).

Assuming those two items are inserted, we are ready to sign. Please send a DocuSign envelope and copy legal@acme-payments.com on the envelope.

DocuSign envelope stub: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123 (placeholder — please replace with live envelope)

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Reynolds
